utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the Trial Chamber's earlier recordings were that Rule 66(B) material does not have to be provided in hard copy to the accused. It does pose a major strain on the Office of the Prosecutor to transcribe these sort of things. What I would propose to do is we'll review these tapes; and if we identify any exculpatory material, then we will comply with the Trial Chamber's direction on how we handle the disclosure of that kind of material. And if the material is relevant but not exculpatory, then we provide it in electronic form to the accused. I believe that's what the Trial Chamber has directed; and, of course, we will undertake that exercise with these recordings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Now, as far as the Rule 66 is concerned, we face the following situation: The accused is representing himself. This grant -- this right was granted to him by the Appeals Chamber. So this is final. Rule 66 in electronic format works fine when there is a lawyer who is conversant in English and French, the working languages of this Tribunal. The accused only wishes to work in his language. So he is entitled to have this document in his own language. Therefore, that is my position on the matter. In light of the rights of the Defence, he is entitled to have a hard copy version of the document, all the more so that he does not wish to use a computer. You can't force an accused to use a computer. So he is perfectly entitled to have a hard copy of this document. That has always been my position. This refers to Rule 66, Rule 66. But for the time being, we are actually discussing Rule 68. This is a document which is pursuant to Rule 68, so he should have this document. He should have a hard copy of this document, and a document in his own language. Otherwise, what situation would we face? Well, we would be in the situation where accused is representing himself. He has no knowledge or is not computer literate, does not wish to use a computer, and therefore cannot defend himself, which would be a serious breach of the rights of the accused. So, before addressing 66(B), let's see whether, according to Rule 68, there are any exculpatory elements in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. We will review these recordings to determine whether there's anything exculpatory in this material. I do believe that it's the Prosecution's obligation to determine whether or not Rule 68 is applicable, of course under the ultimate supervision of the Trial Chamber. But it is not because the accused alleges that a document is exculpatory that it necessarily is. In light of -- I have taken note of what the accused has said, and we will review the tape and treat it in accordance with the directions that the Trial Chamber has already given on this issue. And I would note that there have been earlier discussions, I think, about the option of providing the accused with a language assistant who can help him with these sort of things, and it might be another option for the Trial Chamber to consider. But anyway, we will, for starts, review the document for Rule 68 or exculpatory material.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President. The whole statement is relevant, because General Zivota Panic was the commander of the 1st Military District, and he was in command of the operations. It's not the Supreme Command, but he had the command over the operations in Vukovar and the entire area of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. So it was Sector South and Sector North that were under his command, and everything he said that is exceptionally relevant. I state, I claim that it is, indeed, exculpatory material for me; and with my very own eyes, I have seen one paragraph of that statement, where he confirms that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party were exclusively JNA and so on. Although, we were in a major conflict, the two of us, we even had lawsuits in the court in Belgrade. I was the main person responsible for removing him from the post he occupied. So everything that the Prosecutor says now doesn't stand. They must provide it on paper for me so that I can use it in my cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor will look into this and then things will seem much clearer. Well, this is not an urgent matter to see what General Panic said, but I agree here with what Mr. Seselj said. As he was the commander of the 1st District in charge of the operational zone of Vukovar, this is a person who played a part at the time. Therefore, what he said at the time is particularly relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. The accused has, of course, the transcript of the testimony of the general in the Milosevic case. The accused has still not answered whether he will accept, for starts, in light of the urgency he says this has, a DVD of these recordings. We will provide them; and then, as already undertaken, we will review this material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall give him the floor, but I know what he is about to say. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am astounded by what is happening now. The Prosecutor just tells you that the general testified in the Milosevic trial. That is just not true. General Zivota Panic never testified in evidence a single trial at The Hague Tribunal because he didn't want to do so. He's an honourable man, too honourable and decent to appear as the Prosecution witness against his comrade in arms, but he presented the truth as he saw it. So let's not have this situation happen again. I'm very sorry that you think that I am obstructing the proceedings, but the Prosecution has just told you that General Panic testified in the Milosevic trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, did General Panic testify in the Milosevic case, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry. I might have been mixing up two generals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This can happen; and a while ago, I did mix up two people. So he didn't testify. Right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you briefly describe: Were local Serb Territorial Defence units established in -- in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, such units were established.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to Articles that were published in the SRS party magazine, Velika Srbija, already, not later than April 1991, units of SRS volunteers joined -- moved to Eastern Slavonia to join local Serb defences in several villages and towns located in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were the local TOs in the area subordinated to the JNA; and, if so, from what time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in -- in April 1991, there is no generalised conflict yet, so the JNA is not participating in the fighting. What Eastern Slavonia is concerned, it's only after the incidents in Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May, 1992, that JNA units of the 17th Corps are sent to separate the two parties in Borovo Selo, even though there are barricades erected by local Serbs and local Croats throughout Eastern Slavonia. And, more specifically, where Vukovar is concerned, there the conflict only starts at the end of August, early September, when the JNA units of the 1st Military District start operations to what they call liberate the barracks in Vukovar which have been blocked or surrounded by Croats in the course of the month of August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And during the operation in Vukovar, were the local Territorial Defence and volunteer units operating under the command of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. For what Operational Group South is concerned, local Serb TO, including SRS volunteers, were operating under the command of Operational Group South until at least the 21st of November at 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in binder number 2, there is a document that I would like to discuss with the witness. It is 65 ter number 688. The document is also up in e-court now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is this and document you refer to in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I refer to this document in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And this is an order, a document dated on the 18th of November, and who have issued the document or the order?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The order is issued by the commander of the 1st Military District, Lieutenant-General Zivota Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What was the situation in -- in Vukovar at this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at that time, the Croatian forces in Vukovar have surrendered; and in the order, Panic gives instructions on, first, the taking of control of the hospital of Vukovar, as well as the attitude the armed forces -- I mean, his forces, the JNA, the volunteers, and the TO, have to take now that Vukovar has been, as he calls it, liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, at the second page of the English version, and it's on page 1 of the B/C/S version, you will see the reference to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, are you aware whether there were any agreement about evacuation of civilians from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. There had been evacuations at an earlier stage. Now, there was also an agreement signed in Zagreb on the evacuation of Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this particular agreement is, I believe, and I'm going to ask the witness if it is, Exhibit number -- 65 ter number, sorry, 687. That is the first document that is found in the blue thin folder that was distributed to Your Honours. Maybe we can call it up in e-court, so we can all see it. I realise we have a lot of different folders and binders with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, now that we have it on the screen is this the agreement or order that you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And would you describe the general contents of the agreement for us?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the agreement establishes the conditions for the evacuation of Vukovar Hospital. It establishes also the attitude the JNA has to take; as well, the agreement also defines the role the ICRC, so the International Red Cross, as well as the ECMM, the EC observers, have during the evacuation. If we go to the bottom of the document, we can see who signed it. The signature for the Republic of Croatia is the signature of Mr. Hebrang who was the Minister of Health. There is also the signature of General Andrija Raseta who was the senior negotiator for the JNA, and I'm not sure if any members of ICRC or another NGO signed the agreement too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And how do you know that the signatures are from the people you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I'm familiar with this document from my work on other cases in -- at the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like now to move briefly to two other documents that are related to the situation in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry for interrupting you. Something has escaped me, but what is the date of this last document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you go to the top of the document, there should be a date, because I don't remember the date by heart, whether it's the 16th, the 17th, or the 18th of November, when the agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think if Your Honour look just above --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- above the top signature, you will say it says "18/11/1991." One of the persons who signed it also put the date of signature on the document. Your Honours, we've been talking about volunteers that were present around this time in Vukovar; and for that reason, I thought we should just have a look at 65 ter number 590. It's a brief document. It's back again in binder number 2, and it's a document after the one of we just looked at in this -- in this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you tell us briefly what -- what this document is? I believe you mentioned it yesterday in court as well.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. It's a handwritten letter signed by a person named Filipovic, on what is called the legalisation of the detachment Leva Supoderica. Now that we're at the Vukovar TO staff, I would like to make a correction to what I mentioned yesterday. I mentioned that Slobodan Katic had been removed at one moment as the person in charge of the TO for Vukovar, local Serb TO of Vukovar. I actually confused the name or the name of Katic with the name of Dusan Jaksic. It was Dusan Jaksic who was initially head of the local Serb TO Vukovar and at one time is replaced by a decision of the command of OG South by Miroljub Vujovic. So it was not Katic, but Jaksic I meant yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if you follow two --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I made an objection earlier on, but I don't think it was met with a claim. Now I see that the witness is putting himself right on that score. So I couldn't resist drawing your attention to that, because Katic is the Serbian Radical Party; whereas, Dusan Jaksic never had anything to do with the Serbian Radical Party. This is perhaps a little improper on my part, but I just could not resist pointing that out to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for things to be extremely clear with respect to future objections, please note that the issue is that we are not dismissing your objections. The problem is that these are not objections. You're just taking the floor to talk about the substance of the testimony, and you're quite entitled to do so but not now during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But in this particular case, your objection stands, because if there's a confusion in the names of certain individuals, if you find that there is a mistake by the witness, the Judges, or the Prosecutor, and that can happen, please notify us immediately. But as my fellow Judge has just said, if your objection relates to the substance of the document, then you have to wait until cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If Your Honours would follow with me in the binder two tabs in, two tabs further, sorry, to 65 ter number 707, which is also MFI P41. We, again, have a document reference has been made to a number of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is, I believe, a document that you refer to in your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I refer to this document in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And what conclusion do you draw from this as to the presence of volunteers in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this order signed, it is not signed by Mrksic, it is signed by his Chief of Staff Miodrag Panic. It shows that the Leva Supoderica Detachment, a volunteer detachment, is subordinated to OG South until at least the 21st of November, 1991, at 6.00 in the morning, which shows that Leva Supoderica is also subordinated to the guards, but to OG South, during the events in Ovcara, during the night of the 20th and the 21st of November. The document also shows that, in paragraph 4, other Vukovar TO units are to be resubordinated from OG South to the 80th Motorised Brigade. Again, this is to be executed in the course of the 21st of November. And this is logical from the military point of view because after the fall of Vukovar, the Guards Motorised Brigade is preparing to return to Belgrade; whereas, the 80th Motorised Brigade will stay and take over the command in the area. A last point of interest in the document is the addressee list on the top of the second page in English, where the addressees are identified. And the first addressee is the commander of the Seseljevci Volunteers Detachment, which supports what we discussed yesterday, i.e., that SRS volunteer units or detachments have their own hierarchical structure when they are participating in the fighting and their own commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think, before we forget, I'd like to ask for the admission of the documents we've just been looking at. So I request the admission of 65 ter numbers 688; 687; 590; 957; 707, which is also MFI 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. 65 ter 688 will be Exhibit number P248. 65 ter number 687 will be Exhibit number P24. 65 ter number 590 will be Exhibit number 250. 65 ter number 957 will be Exhibit number P251. 65 ter number 707 will be Exhibit number P41.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, based on the material you have reviewed, were there concerns in the JNA hierarchy about crimes being committed by volunteers in the Vukovar area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Such concerns existed at the time of the events, as well as afterwards; and, actually, the Panic order we discussed earlier for the 18th of November, 1991, in which reference was made to taking over the hospital, explicitly refers to unsoldierly behaviour and acts of retribution, including by members of the local Serb TO prior to the issuing of that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And Mr. Theunens, and Your Honours, if you would turn with me to the tab which has 65 ter number 604.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We have an urgent telegram to the commander of the 1st Military Distinct dated the 23rd of October, 1991. So I believe that would be before the events we just talked about.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. This document has been signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Milan Eremija, who is the assistant commander for morale and political guidance in the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division, and he sends a report on the morale situation among the forces of the PGMD.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if we could go to the second -- if we go to the second page, item number 4, and maybe in particular the last bullet point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is this something you have referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I have referred to it. This is in the report because it's relevant for the matters that are discussed in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And this states that: "In the combat activities zone of the 1st PGM, the main motive behind the presence of several groups of different paramilitary formations from Serbia, Chetniks, the Dusan Silni Detachment, and various self-styled volunteers is not to combat but to loot people's property and engage in sadistic abuse of innocent civilians of Croatian nationality." Mr. Theunens, have you been -- do you have an opinion on what is meant by the reference to "Chetniks"?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, the question of relevance imposes itself here. There's no mention of the volunteers of the Serb Radical Movement, so it is misplaced to discuss this document. If we do that, then we would have to discuss all the crimes that took place in this war on that same basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. It did not escape me. I noticed that the SRS volunteers were not mentioned. That's why it was so interesting to put that question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Eremija makes reference or uses the term "Chetniks. " Now, from the documents we have discussed over the previous days, we have noticed that it's actually the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party who used the name Chetnik not only to identify themselves but also to identify their detachment or units; and the term "Chetnik" is also being used by the Serbian Radical Party War Staff in that context. I am well aware that members of the other parties involved in the conflict, like the Croats or the Muslims/Bosniaks, sometimes use the term "Chetnik" in a -- in a general way, the same way as the Serbs use the term "Ustasha" or even other derogatory terms for the other side. However, if a senior officer who is responsible for morale and political guidance sends a report of this nature to the superior command, I think one can have confidence in the fact that he makes sure that the information he includes in his report is correct, that he has checked the facts, and that he is also accurate in the names of individuals, locations, factions, groups he includes in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if Your Honours would follow me to the next document, it will shed some more light on this issue I presume, I hope. The next document is 65 ter number 649, and it is the next document in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we move on to this document, the legal officer has just reminded me that you asked for the admission of 65 ter 957. It was admitted under P251, but you actually never showed this document to the witness before requesting its admission. Document 957 was never put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did I request -- sorry. That is an error and I am grateful to the court officers for this. I skipped the document, and did not cross it out. I do not intend to tender it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So we'll withdraw this document from the exhibit list. Mr. Registrar, please remove Exhibit P251 from the list of exhibits mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, 65 ter number 649, Mr. Theunens, this is a document that's referred to in your report. Could you briefly explain from who to who this document has -- what this document is? Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is, as the title says, a periodical operations report of the -- "OB" stands for security organs of the Guards Motorised Brigade. It is submitted to the security administration at the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence, and it's signed by the assistant Chief of Cabinet at the SSNO, the assistant chief for security, Lieutenant-Colonel Dragoljub Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if we go to the second page of the document, there is a specific reference to the Vukovar operation. You will see it says: "With regards to the Vukovar operation, the Serbian nationalistic and the Chetnik propaganda are taking a serious dimension which in its breadth outstrips by far the results in the combat of the volunteers and the paramilitary units. The nationalistic and ideological symbols, nationalistic sons, the speeches of Vojislav Seselj, the liquidation of POWs by Chetniks, et cetera, are unjustifiably tolerated. "We point to the legitimacy of the silence -- sorry, acknowledgement of the legitimacy of the Chetnik commanding officers, the existence of Serbian volunteer groups as established units, and requests to designate such compositions to a special axis and tasks." Mr. Theunens, have you quoted this in your report at well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document is, if I'm not wrong, included in the addendum to my report because it became available after March 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, in the translation, there is included the title of officers, I believe it is. It's "staresina." Are you familiar with that term?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my understanding the term "staresina" means actually that it's superior. It means superior. It doesn't have to be an officer. It's just a person in a superior position in the military concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, is this one of the documents that you have considered also in -- in finding out what is meant by "Chetniks"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. It's the same reply I gave earlier that one can expect that the security organ at the level of the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence knows very well what it is talking about, and that it's not -- that it has checked the information, verified the information before forwarding it to the superior because the superior is -- is using this information to base his decisions on. So the information has to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if we go back to the first page, just to see the date of the document. The document is dated on the 7th of November, 1991. So that would have been before the takeover of Vukovar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I request the admission of 65 ter numbers 604 and 649.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 604 will be Exhibit P251, and 65 ter number 649 will be Exhibit number P252.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One question on this document, please. It is sent to the cabinet of the Federal Secretariat for the National Defence. So this document is going to be extremely high in the military hierarchy, up to the top; and General Kadijevic is probably going to know about it. The Vukovar operation is mentioned here, and it is stated here that the Chetniks have liquidated the POWs; and here there is a question as to nationalism, the anthem, the speeches, and so on. So this seems to be a very negative document. Is it the only one the of the kind that you've seen, or have you seen others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I have also seen other documents, and the most relevant ones are included in the report. In this context, I can mention 65 ter number 985, which is included in the addendum to the report. 65 ter 985 is a report compiled by a commission which was established for the clearing of the battlefield after the end of military operations. It means that dead bodies have to be removed, unexploded ammunition has to be removed, the terrain has to be cleaned, and so on. There --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. Could you help me and tell me the following: Who exactly wrote this report? I mean, it is signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Djukic, but what unit does this person belong to, please? Who does this Djukic report to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Djukic is a member of the cabinet of the Federal Secretariat of People's Defence where he works as the assistant chief for security. The information he uses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So he is in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. But if you allow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he's referring to the Vukovar operation. It is probably because he has received a number of reports.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours. That can also be derived from the first page, the title of the document, where it says that it's, under the date reference, it's a periodical operations report of the OB, so security organs of the Guards Motorised Brigade. I can explain this by making a reference to what I said earlier that these are the Guards Motorised Brigade who were normally subordinated to the SSNO through the Chief of Cabinet of the SSNO. And this document shows that even though the Guards Motorised Brigade on the 30th of September was resubordinated to the 1st Military District, when the Guards Motorised Brigade was sent to Vukovar, the security organs of the Guards Motorised Brigade still continued to send reports to the security organs of their higher echelon in peacetime, i.e., the security organs at the SSNO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But isn't there a contradiction in -- in military terms? I mean, this is a report that is highly critical of the militaries and the paramilitary and the volunteers --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Volunteers and paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even though we know they took part in military operations. So it seems that they have found out that crimes were committed against POWs, and can't this be seen as an attempt to try and blame someone else for this? It could be envisaged, you know, in terms of military matters. It seems that they have found out that unjustifiable acts were committed, which is what is written here, and isn't this an attempt to try and blame this on others --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- find a scapegoat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My conclusion from reading this report and analysing it - it's in contents of the other documents I reviewed, and most of them are included in the report - actually shows that within the JNA, there are people at the senior level who don't do -- who don't disagree with the acceptance of volunteers; and I mean by that political volunteers, so volunteers who operate in separate units and who essentially a political motivation or even an ethnical motivation to participate in the conflict. So there are senior officers who do not agree with the fact that this is all being permitted and that these volunteers are then allowed to do the things they are doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, one last question. In this document, Arkan is also challenged, you know, when he attends the funeral of General Bratic. I have no idea who this General Bratic is, but it says he should not have -- in the presence of General -- his presence at the funeral of General Bratic was unjustifiably emphasised on. There is a critical of Arkan and his competence also, obviously. So what happened to this General Bratic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Bratic was the first commander of Operational Group South. And during the first week of October 1991, I believe that he was, if I remember well, he was hit by a grenade, but I'm not sure exactly when it happened. So I'm not sure whether it happened in October. Anyway, he was hit by a grenade and he was killed, which means that he was replaced; and if I remember well, he was replaced by Biorcevic as the commander of OG North. Now, the criticism on Arkan is also in first instance directed to that fact that in the public, i.e., the state-controlled media, there is a lot of attention for the volunteers and even positive attention, including positive attention for Arkan where, according to this report, Arkan is allowed to give his assessment on the way how the Vukovar operation is being conducted, and also that Arkan is giving -- is given a stage to -- yeah, to express his views in relation to the military operations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A brief objection, Your Honour, Mr. President. I heard that the witness said that General Bratic was the first commander of OG South. That's how it was interpreted to me. Then he says that he was replaced by General Biorcevic who was the commander of OG South. In this galimatias, I cannot find my way around in this word salad. So can we clarify this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems, apparently, that there is a little mistake regarding the person who replaced General Bratic, that he would have been replaced by the commander of Operational Group North. Can you please tell us exactly what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I made an error when I started to reply the question. Bratic was the commander of OG North, so it's not South. Then he was replaced by Biorcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This was a well-grounded objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed. Your Honours, the next topic I'll move on to is Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, under which JNA forces, did Western Slavonia fall?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Western Slavonia was located in the zone of responsibility of the 5th JNA Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the 5th JNA Corps came under which military district?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's still the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And from the documents you have seen, were Territorial Defence set up -- were Territorial Defence units set up in Western Slavonia in the same way that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My microphone is on but I have no light. Maybe I can use the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I pressed the button that cuts everything off by mistake. Always by mistake. I will never cut anybody's microphone off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm sure, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Theunens, were Territorial Defence units established in Western Slavonia? And here I mean Serb Territorial Defence units.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honours. I discuss a document that provides an overview of the structure of the local Serb Territorial Defence on page 126 in the report, and that's actually P181.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When were these units established, approximately?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Your Honours, that's a gradual progress but it intensifies in fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And were these Territorial Defence units, were they subordinated to the JNA; and, if so, from when?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Orders are issued. For example, I have an order on the 31st of October, 1991, by Colonel Talic, commander of the 5th JNA Corps, stating that all local Serb TO units and staffs are subordinated to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And we have been through this maybe a number of times, but were there also SRS/SCP volunteers operating in this area around this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. We see that various local Serb municipalities in Western Slavonia during fall 1991 contact the SRS War Staff in order to request manpower and also the assistance of -- in some cases -- excuse me, in some cases assistance of the War Staff of the SRS to provide weapons or equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just as a cross-reference, for future review of the transcripts, we have in particular discussing earlier on 65 ter numbers 570, 582, 594, and 609, which are relevant to this particular topic. I'm not going to go into that much further. I would like to go back to an issue that came up with another witness on the 12th of February, transcript pages 300 -- no, sorry, 3422 to 3447. There was a discussion, a discussion of Exhibit P187, and, Your Honours, that document is also 65 ter number 1026, and it is the last document that's included in the blue folder that we had up just before. If we can call up the exhibit in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I believe you discussed this document in your report, and the issue of the gentleman of the name of Kulic Jovanovic -- Jovana. Now, there is, in this document, mention of some military post numbers. Could you explain to us first what they are?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military post numbers are numbers that identify units. So each unit has a military post number, and this is the military post number for a JNA unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And based on your review of documentary material, have you formed a view about who Jovan Kulic is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. This document identifies, the one we're seeing, Jovan Kulic as a self-appointed captain 1st class. Now, an article that was published in issue number 12 of Velika Srbija, so the SRS party magazine, states that Jovan Kulic was a member of the Kragujevac Chetnik Detachment, and also the commander of the defence of the village of Petrova Slatina, which is located in Western Slavonia. The 65 ter number there would be 958.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if you have it, maybe we can call it up in e-court. And in the binder --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Judge, sir. I feel it's completely impermissible for this kind of forgery to be presented here. The OTP has submitted Velika Srbija number 12. We see on page 56, it says Jovan Kulic, reserve JNA captain, volunteer from Novi Sad, commander of the defence of the village of Petrova Slatina; and yet we saw yesterday and the day before yesterday that Srecko Radosavljevic said that this person was not a member of a SRS volunteer unit but someone with whom there was cooperation. That was presented here yesterday. You can look at it on page 56. It says he's from Novi Sad. If there's an error stating that he's from Kragujevac, he can't be both from Novi Sad and Kragujevac. But in the criminal report, it says he's from Novi Sad. It says the volunteer unit from Novi Sad, and the witness himself told you that in addition to the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, there are were two companies of unidentified volunteers from Novi Sad, to the TO Novi Sad. That's what it said. I think I had to point out this attempt to pass off a forgery here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Witness, as you're an expert, the document is a report sent to the military prosecutor, and this document relates to breaches of Article 151 of the criminal procedure applied at the time. This concerns Kulic who seemingly comes from Novi Sad. This would be location he came from. Who commanded the volunteers unit of Novi Sad? Seemingly, he's a conscript; and, as you mentioned, he reports to the 8316th structure of the JNA. In other words, he's a military man, and that is why he needs to report to the military prosecutor. Otherwise, this would be a civilian prosecutor. So this person is a military person. Does he report to Novi Sad? Which volunteers are we talking about, volunteers the SRS or other political parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the reference I have made, at an earlier stage, to a volunteer unit from Novi Sad was in context of Vukovar, where we discussed an order from the command of OG South where the Novi Sad volunteer company was mentioned as one of the units in the 1st Assault Detachment. So it's a different area. In relation to this particular document, the fact that he is a conflict does not exclude that he's a volunteer. What I mean by that is that among the volunteers were actually many people who should have been conscripts; but for political reasons or other reasons, they refused to serve in the JNA and preferred to be a volunteer in a separate volunteer unit with their own symbols and their own ideology. All I did, when looking at this criminal report, was to try to find out who are these people. Who is Jovan Kulic? Who is Ane Milosevic, and so on and so on, the other people mentioned in the document. Then I tried to identify these people. And in relation to Jovan Kulic, there's not only the SRS Velika Srbija article, but also 65 ter number 933, which states or repeats that Kulic is a self-proclaimed captain who robbed and looted in Western Slavonia. There is also a statement included in the report, in my report, a statement made by Kulic to the Secretary of the Interior in Novi Sad, and that's 65 ter number 1693, in which Kulic explains where he was and when he was there. And it's correct that, in this statement, he doesn't make a reference to the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what conclusions must we draw? Is he a member of the SRS or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My conclusion, Your Honour, is that unless the Jovan Kulic who is referred to in the Velika Srbija is a totally different person, then we're talking about one individual who is a member of the Kragujevac Chetnik Detachment, unless the article in Velika Srbija is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this might be an issue that you will have to determine, decide on later on in making your findings. I was going to tender the two document -- two of the documents that the witness have just mentioned; namely, 933 and 958, which are included here. The witness have already described what they are. So we propose they be given a number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 958 will be Exhibit number P253 and 65 ter number 933 will be Exhibit number P254.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I now move to -- sorry, Your Honours. Am I correct we have ten minutes to the next break or are we running overtime?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Ten minutes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Merci. Your Honours, I am moving to the situation on the ground in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in part 2 of your report at page 146, and that is page 276 in the B/C/S version, you discuss the deployment of the JNA after the Vance Plan. Could you please tell us where the JNA deployed when they left Croatia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, one of the aspects of the Vance-Owen Plan is the demilitarisation of the area covered by the UN peace forces, including the withdrawal of the JNA. So JNA units from Croatia withdraw to Bosnia-Herzegovina even though personnel and equipment is -- is left behind. And at the same time, because of the withdrawal or the official withdrawal from Croatia, the 1st Military District is -- the zone of responsibility is redefined. And the 2nd Military District is established whereby the 2nd Military District, which starts to function on the 10th of January, 1992, covers the largest part of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now that you mention that personnel and equipment was left behind, who was this -- who was this left with?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, personnel of the JNA who were born in -- in the Krajina or other areas in Croatia were allowed to stay. Now, I know, from reviewing other documents, that also people were forced to stay or to serve in the RSK TO which was transformed into the police and then transformed into the SVK. The same happened with military equipment. I'm not claiming that all the military equipment was left behind, but significant numbers of -- or amount military equipment was left behind for the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The JNA units that went to Bosnia-Herzegovina, were they deployed in -- in areas with a certain ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. In the report, I make mention of a document; and if I'm not wrong, it's an order by Adzic whereby units and also equipment of the JNA, which is located in areas with a non-Serb majority, is moved or is redeployed to areas with a Serb majority. It's a order by Adzic or a report by Kukanjac, General Kukanjac, who was commander of the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: At the time in the winter of 1991, were there already concerns about the possible military consequences of recognition -- of international recognition of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. These concerns existed among other people with Borisav Jovic, the outgoing chairman of the SFRY president circumstances, as well as General Kadijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And what was the concern more specifically?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a realisation that, now that Croatia was gone, that Bosnia-Herzegovina would go the same way. The JNA had learned from its experiences in Croatia, and efforts were made to make sure that the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina could be assisted in pursuing their goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And what steps were taken, what things were being considered in the winter of 1991? You described that, I believe, just for reference, at page 148 of your report, and that's B/C/S pages 277, 278.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I make reference to notes Jovic makes in his diary, published diary, referring to a conversation on the 5th of December, 1991, where, according to Jovic, Milosevic, Slobodan Milosevic, suggests to withdraw all JNA members who were born in Serbia and Montenegro from BiH, and to return all JNA members who have been born in BiH to BiH, so to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was a concern about enabling the Serb population in Bosnia-Herzegovina to -- to defend themselves.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you quote on paragraph 148 from Mr. Jovic's notes, and there's a passage which say that in that situation, that is in case the JNA would have to withdraw, the Serb populace in Bosnia-Herzegovina which has not created its own paramilitary units will be left defenceless and under threat. Were steps taken to organise the Serb populace in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Such steps were taken with a major role played by the Serbian Democratic Party, SDS, as well as elements of the JNA 2nd Military District, and whereby the SDS relied on support from Serbia, more specifically the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who were the leaders of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most -- the most or the best known senior members of the SDS were Radovan Karadzic [Realtime transcript read in error "Kadijevic"], Momcilo Krajisnik, Biljana Plavsic, Nikola Koljevic. But I'm not sure who was the party president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On line 2 of page 75, there's a mistake. Its he not Radovan "Kadijevic," but Radovan "Karadzic."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm looking at the watch and realise that we might have hit another break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we shall have a break now. I believe you have 20 to 30 minutes left, no more than that. The registrar will let us know. So we shall conclude the examination-in-chief today. This is most important, because we need to start on the cross-examination next week. We shall now have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you mentioned that in the setting up of Serb TOs in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia rendered support. What kind of support did they give?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That support consisted -- consisted mainly of -- of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did the JNA assist in the setting up of the TOs as well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and that can be derived from several sources. There are documents from the 2nd Military District, in particular reports compiled -- a report compiled by the commander, Kukanjac, as well as from reports of the VRS, for example, the 1992 analysis of combat readiness report which is mentioned and which is discussed in the report, my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You've earlier mentioned that volunteers were sent by the SRS/SCP to Bosnia-Herzegovina. When -- when did that begin? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have included a reference to an authorisation given by the chief of the SRS War Staff to Nikodin Cavic, and this dates from the 13th of December, 1991. But that concerns volunteers from Bosnia-Herzegovina who wish to participate in the conflict in Croatia. Otherwise, I have no specific date, except the dates that are mentioned when discussing the various locations that I discussed in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so that is that there are -- we will get to this, but there were volunteers involved around the time of the takeovers of the different areas that you discussed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in light of the time, I'm going to jump a number of documents, but there's one document I think that Your Honours may wish to have a look at later. It is Exhibit 65 ter number 1023, and it is again in binder number 2, sort of one-third in or there about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please ask the witness if he knew this document, if he included the document in his report without going into any detailed analysis of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. I was just allowing everyone to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is this a document you have referred to? It is conclusions of the evaluation of the BiH territory in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at page 6 of this document, you will see something that's also mentioned in the expert report. I believe there you have an overview of volunteers, the number of volunteers, and distribution of weapons by the JNA and the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So I thought Your Honours would want to have this simply to get a feel for the numbers and sizes of volunteers in this area. Your Honours, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One very brief question. We see here, in this 2nd Military District, that allegedly there were 69.198 volunteers. But I was just checking the date of the proclamation of the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the date of the withdrawal of the JNA. It's on the 6th of April, 1992 that the United States and the European Community recognised Bosnia and Herzegovina. As of the 6th of April, the JNA -- JNA had no reason to remain there on the ground, and that's why I'm asking the following: They had no legal reason to be there, but still they set up the 2nd Military District. Do you have any explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 2nd military district becomes operational on the 10th of January, 1992. So there is still a significant amount of time between, on one hand, the date when the 2nd Military District becomes operational and, on the other hand, the recognition by, as you mentioned, the United States and the European Community on -- of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But as of the month of April, as of the 6th of April, was the 2nd Military District removed? Did it cease to exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 2nd Military District started its withdrawal, if I remember well, in the course of the month of April; and for example, in some areas, the withdrawal results in incidents. The incidents in early May 1992 when JNA units in Sarajevo tried to leave the barracks there and they are intercepted or ambushed by forces under the control of the BiH government are very well known. So, at any rate anyway, the withdrawal is a gradual process. So it's not dissolved on the 6th of April. It continues to exist, but it starts to withdraw, which also includes the handing over of equipment -- the redeployment of equipment and then the handing over of equipment to local Serb TO and subsequently the VRS, as well as the transfer of personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just to make a reference back to what we talked about earlier, at page 148 of the report, we talked about Jovic's notes. And you will see that, in the last part of what the witness has quoted there from the notes, it says that -- it talks about this -- preparing for this situation, and notes that steps will be taken which will allow for the local Serbs to take over part of the command of the JNA or the remains thereof. Just to tie this in again as the context for the creation of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one question about that. Did the volunteers gradually withdraw from Bosnia and Herzegovina together with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to clarify, the number given by Kukanjac does not indicate where these volunteers are from. They may also be locals. To answer your question, no, I haven't seen any -- any information that would suggest that these volunteers, I mean the volunteers coming from outside Bosnia-Herzegovina, withdrew. On the contrary, from the areas I discussed in the report, we see that, even after April 1992, volunteers continued to participate in the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, when volunteer units came in from outside Bosnia-Herzegovina to the area, did they operate within certain structures that were already existing on the ground in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I cannot give a -- a short answer to that question because it all depends of the area we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were they -- were they sometimes involved, particularly during the takeovers, were they operating together with the TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. When we look at the different areas, particularly the takeovers in Northern Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bijeljina, Zvornik, Brcko, Bosanski Samac, and other areas, we see that volunteers are not operating as an isolated entity, but they are operating together with sometimes forces of the local Serb TO, forces of the local Serb police, sometimes even forces of the TO Serbia, units of the JNA, in some cases even members of the special unit of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. This kind of -- the composition of the forces really depends of -- of the area we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, you -- you discuss in your report the so-called six strategic goals. That is at page 155 and in the B/C/S version 286. Was the organisation and arming of the TO in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in your view, a result of these goals?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, even though these six strategic goals are only publicly announced on the 12th of May, 1992, we see that a number of takeovers of municipalities that actually serve the accomplishment of these goals have taken place long before the goals are announced. However, when we look at the goals and we see how they are translated into military documents, there is -- there is coherence. Not only for the operational instructions or operational directives the VRS is to issue between May 1992 and May 1995, but also the takeovers, they follow a certain logic. It is not by coincidence that a particular municipality is taken over. One would only commit forces to achieve a particular goal and a political goal; and, obviously, the political goal corresponds with the goals that are specified or included in the section strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the Variant A and B decision?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not included those in my report, but I've known -- I know of it but I wouldn't be able to present them in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But, in general, do you have a view on whether or not this Variant A and B is also tied in with these takeovers and the six strategic goals that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours, because there needs to be coherence on the -- on the political and military level. The six strategic goals are the highest instructions that are given by the political leadership to the military. It is up to the military then to implement these strategic goals. Again as I said, I think that the date that they became public is not -- is not the essential element here. The fact that we can link the takeovers to the goals allows us to better understand what the goals mean and why it was important to implement them. And the same applies to Variant A and Variant B.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in light of the time, I propose to move on to a brief discussion of the individual sites or locations in Bosnia-Herzegovina that are treated in the expert report, and the first of these is Bijeljina, which is discussed -- discussion begins at page 171 of the English version, which is page 306 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what was the strategic importance of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through its location, Bijeljina or the takeover of Bijeljina serves the following goals: First of all, it is located at what is called or it's located at the entrance of what became known as the Posavina corridor, which is literally translated corridor in the valley of the Sava, which connected the RSK and the western part of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and later the RS, with Serbia. The takeover also served the strategic goal which consisted of the elimination of the Drina as a border. And, thirdly, also served the goal, the first strategic goal, which consisted of separation of the ethnic groups or the people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Which JNA units were in the area of Bijeljina around the time of the takeover?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th Corps, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And were there also -- were there volunteer formations in the area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Based on the documents I reviewed, Bijeljina was taken over by members of the group known as Arkan Tigers, as well as a group of SRS volunteers led by Mirko Blagojevic. There were also groups of the SDS and other armed formations that participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Have you been able to determine whether any JNA forces participated in the takeover?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, according to a report, Colonel Savo Jankovic, the commander of the 17th Corps, since on the 3rd of April to the commander of the 2nd Military District, Arkan prevented armoured units of the 17th Corps to enter Bijeljina. So to answer the question, I've seen reports where the 17th Corps provides information on the situation in Bijeljina, but I haven't seen reports where from which it can be determined that units of the JNA participated in the actual takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Based on the documents of reviewed, did the volunteer units remain in Bijeljina after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I refer, therefore, for that aspect, to reports that are compiled by the Bosnian Serb Bijeljina security service centre, also known as SJB. This, for example, is report of the 29th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And in the documentation you have reviewed, are there indications that -- that the JNA and other structures were concerned about crimes being committed by, in particular, if we can talk about SRS/SCP volunteers in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SJB report of the 29th of July, 1992, which is 65 ter number 1525, talks about paramilitary groups, in the first place, the Serbian volunteer guard, i.e., Arkan Tigers, but does not provide information on any involvement of the Serbian Radical Party volunteers. Then, of course, I have statements made by Mirko Blagojevic. One is from a press conference, 65 ter number 1032, where he states that there was no massacre whatsoever against the Muslim population, especially not by members of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've also then have VRS report which talks about -- it's 65 ter number 1523, which talks about a conflict between a unit known as the so-called guards and the members of the Radical Party led by Mirko Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm speeding off Bijeljina to go to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Theunens, the same sort of series of questions --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but how much more time does the Prosecutor have, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He should have about 20 minutes left. Mr. Registrar, can you please check that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, ten minutes to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, ten minutes. Yes. I was too generous.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Theunens, the strategic importance of Zvornik, what was the strategic importance? Was that similar to that of Bijeljina or are there any differences?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The takeover of Zvornik serves the same strategic goals as in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In this case were JNA forces involved in the takeover based on the documents you've seen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents I've seen show that the JNA is aware of the situation and also reports on the developments in the city, but I have not been able to establish whether the JNA also actively participated in the takeover. The documents I have reviewed identify other forces that carried out the takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And who were -- what are those forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They consist of units of the local Serb TO, which includes also a volunteer formation which became known under the name Yellow Wasps or "Zuta Osa," Arkan Tigers. Then also members of the TO of Loznica. By Loznica is a municipality of Serbia, so on the other side of the border. As well as, according to what Mr. Seselj stated in public, the members of the Special Purpose Unit of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, the SRS --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. I have also been able to establish that an individual known as Zoran Subotic, who in 1993 was reported as a parliamentary representative of the SRS in the Republic of Serbia, participated in the takeover, and, yeah, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, do you have any indication of how the SRS/SCP volunteers that were in the area were brought into the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of these formations, particularly the Yellow Wasps, made statements to local police officials mentioning that they were brought to the area by Zoran Rankic, who we know as the deputy chief of the SRS War Staff in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did -- to your knowledge, were there reports or crimes committed by SRS/SCP volunteers in the Zvornik area during or after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is extensive reporting on -- on the participation of members of the Yellow Wasps and related formations in the commission of crimes during and after the takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In Brcko -- in Bosanski Samac - sorry, moving on - what are the strategic objective or what is the strategic significance of that area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanski Samac is of strategic importance because of its location. It's located on the area that became known as the Posavina corridor; and a takeover of Bosanski Samac also serves the first strategic goal, the separation of the Serbian people from the other people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And based on the review of the -- or review ever documents that you have carried out, what forces participated in the takeover?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These forces consisted of people were known as SRS volunteers, including Srecko Radovanovic, also known as Debeli; Dusan Tozic [phoen], also known as Luis [phoen]. There was also a Sasa Culabrk [phoen], including of course the volunteers who were operating under their command. There was a Chetnik detachment from Kragujevac, and there's also information on the participation of an official of the MUP Serbia, Dragan Djordjevic, also known as Crni.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, again, from this area, are there reports of crimes being committed in the context of the takeover by SCP volunteers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. There is a report of the 2nd Posavina Brigade of VRS, which talks about the role of Dragan Djordjevic and Srecko Radovanovic and the forces operating under their command in the -- in the commission of crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if we move on - I know this is high speed and I apologise, but I think we have to - to Brcko, what strategic objectives were Brcko relevant to -- Brcko relevant to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Brcko is located in the vicinity of Bosanski Samac and by its location controls the Posavina corridor. So the takeover of the Brcko supported the strategic goal consisting of the establishment of a corridor between Semberija and Krajina, and also the goal of the separation of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And what forces participated in the takeover?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents I have reviewed indicate that forces consisting of a unit known as Serbian guard under the command of Ljubisa Cavic, also known as Mauzer; SRS volunteers under the command of Mirko Blagojevic; Arkan Tigers; and also local volunteers trained by Dragan Vasiljevic -- Vasiljkovic, excuse me, Dragan Vasiljkovic, also known as Captain Dragan participated in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, again, in the context of this particular locations, had there reports of crimes being committed during and after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. There was a report which was compiled by the VRS in September 1992 which refers to volunteers operating under the command of Blagojevic; Gavrilovic, so Branislav Gavrilovic, whom I haven't mentioned yet, in the commission of crimes. And I would just like to add that also the proclamation order for Vojvoda dated the 13th of May, 1993, doesn't only mention Blagojevic and Radovanovic but also Mitar Maksimovic, also known as Manda, and Branislav Vakic in relation to their participation in the takeover Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, we now move from the eastern part of BiH to the Sarajevo area. What was the strategic significance of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Radovan Karadzic publicly announced the six strategic goals, he listed the division of Sarajevo as the fifth strategic goal, explaining that in his view, as long as Sarajevo is split, Izetbegovic, so the head or the president of Bosnia-Herzegovina, would not have a state as long as its capital was divided.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And what -- what armed forces have you identified in the Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of the report, the following units are of relevance: We have the VRS corps in the area, which is the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, also known as SRK. As far as the SRS volunteers are concerned, there were four groups. There was group under the command of Mirko Blagojevic, also known as Brne. There was a group under the command of Slavko Aleksic, and this group was also known as the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik Detachment. There was a group under the command of Jovan -- Jovo Ostojic, as well as a group under the command for the -- for Vasiljkovic, also known as Vaske.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Prosecutor, I think your five hours are up, so please, one last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in general, in relation to the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina, are there reports -- are there reports that the SRS volunteers were involved in crimes in the area, and do you have an assessment of the scope of these crimes geographically?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documents I have reviewed, I have, for all the errors included in the report, I have found documents compiled by JNA or VRS or local police officials indicating that members of volunteer formations, including SRS volunteers, were involved in the commission of crimes in the area -- in the areas they were participating in the fighting. These documents are included in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will move for the admission now of the report of the expert and the addendum and the corrigendum to the report. That would be 65 ter number 2854, 2854A, 2854B, 2854C, and then we have redacted versions of the report as well which are 2854D and E -- Sorry, I'm told this is incorrect. Sorry. 2854E is the conversion table that I provided which allow you to find your way between English and B/C/S pages. So these to be the 65 ter numbers for the report. As I mentioned, when the testimony of the witness started, the Prosecution also requests the admission of the underlying exhibits that are used in the report. I think the testimony of the witness have illustrated the importance of the documents that have been used in the report. I have for Your Honours a table - or I will have in a little bit - a table which indicates where each of the exhibits that I referred to in the report are mentioned in the footnotes. So each exhibit number you can see for the relevancy where they are in the report. The hard copy will be brought down to court shortly, but it has been uploaded into e-court as 65 ter number 7111. I say this just so there's a reference for the future to the document. It might also be handy document to have in any event, but I would request the admission of all the exhibits that are included on that list which have not yet been admitted. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have duly noted your requests. We will not rule on this right now. We will wait for Mr. Seselj's position on this, and we will make a decision later on. We have half an hour to go for cross-examination, and I now give the floor to Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, you are an intelligence analyst in The Hague Tribunal for seven years; is that right? You've been one for seven years; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost seven years, Your Honours. In June 2008, it will be seven years.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what is your monthly salary?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- my salary does not depend, first of all, of this report or whether I testify or not. And, secondly, I don't believe that my salary is relevant in the context of my testimony. My salary has no influence on my credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's not talk about monetary amounts, but I'm sure that you are at a certain level. Are you P2, P3, P4? Could you tell us what category you fall under?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm a P3, step 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3, 6. Very good. This is public, then it's very simple. You just have to take a look at the budget of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I insist on having the witness answer my question and tell me how big his salary is. I can't look at the budget of the Tribunal and deduce it that way, but it goes to the credibility of the witness. So could he please answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: With respect, I submit it's irrelevant what his salary is. What his count is and maybe the seniority level in the organisation and that's just been located. His monthly salary is of absolutely no relevance to the issue here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber, after having deliberated, believes we should move on to something else. If Mr. Seselj wants to find out how much this person is making, he just -- there are public documents that he may consult for this. So let's move along.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like the witness to answer the question himself and tell me what his salary is, but I'll have to abide by your ruling. I cannot do otherwise, and I'll move on to my next question. However, I am very disappointed that I'm not allowed to insist that the witness answer my first question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, your main task in the -- in The Hague Tribunal is to provide military support in investigations; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, military support to investigations and prosecutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
